Each entry names a symptom and points to the article that explains it. Where
no article covers a topic yet, the answer is given here.

## My versions don't match an article's, or a colleague's

First compare `data_sha` (`current_data_sha` in `datom_list()`). If it
matches, the values are identical and only the recorded provenance differs;
if it doesn't, the values themselves differ. Both cases are covered in
[Version SHAs](design-version-shas.html):

- *Line endings: the same data, two different files* -- the usual cause when
  a script writes the input files on Windows and on macOS or Linux.
- *One caveat that is not ours to fix* -- reading decimal numbers from text
  can give slightly different values on different machines.
- *Derived columns: when arithmetic breaks cross-platform identity* -- the
  same calculation can give slightly different results on different machines.

## A sync made a new version, but the data didn't change

See *Change classification* in [Version SHAs](design-version-shas.html): a
new source file or new parents make a new version even when the values are
identical.

## `datom_write()` refuses one of my columns

See *The datom table contract* and *The recourse table* in
[Version SHAs](design-version-shas.html). `datom_check_hashable()` checks a
table before you write it.

## `datom_sync()` refuses a file

See *The ingestion allowlist* in [Version SHAs](design-version-shas.html).
